# Lorraine Gaudio

::: {.hero-lead}
I study how AI is reshaping knowledge creation and collective learning in research and education communities.
:::

My research examines how people trust, verify, adapt, reject, and share AI-mediated practices, and how those patterns affect collective intelligence, scientific integrity, and human judgment.

## Current research focus

AI systems are becoming part of how researchers generate ideas, evaluate evidence, make decisions, and learn from one another. I study these changes as features of a larger sociotechnical system involving people, AI tools, institutions, networks, practices, and norms.

Across this work, I ask how AI-mediated practices spread through communities, how people decide when to rely on or question AI, and how repeated interactions may shape collaboration, diversity of knowledge, and scientific self-correction.

Methodologically, I draw on social network analysis, data analytics, and mixed methods. I am also developing computational and agent-based modeling approaches to study human-AI systems over time.
